texts.setting.base_clock.about: The clock the CPU speed is a multiple of. PC-98 machines run either from 2.4576 MHz (the 5 and 10 MHz family) or from 1.9968 MHz (the 8 MHz family). Some old software times itself by it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.clock_multiplier.about: The CPU runs at the base clock times this number. The default of 20 gives 49.152 MHz. A higher number makes the CPU faster and the emulator slower. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.clock_multiplier.about_2: The CPU runs at the base clock times this number. The default of 4 gives 9.8304 MHz, the speed of a real PC-9801VX (the 8 MHz models are 4 with the 1.9968 MHz base clock, the 12 MHz ones 5). Old software that times itself by the CPU runs too fast when it is higher. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.cpu_type.about: Which CPU the IA-32 machine reports to software that asks (the CPUID instruction): its maker, family and the features it has. The default, Intel Pentium III, is the CPU NP2kai starts as. Windows and some PC-9821 software check it, and a few programs refuse a CPU they do not know or crash on features a real PC-9821 never had; an older choice hides the newer features. Neko Processor II is NP2kai's own, with every feature the emulator has. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.dip_switches.about: The three banks of DIP switches on the back of the machine, as three bytes in hexadecimal, bank 1 first (NP2kai writes them the same way in its np2.cfg). The default, 3E E3 7B, is NP2kai's. They tell the BIOS and software things such as the monitor, the number of floppy drives and the memory fitted. Switch 1-1 (the lowest bit of the first byte) is set by the Monitor setting, and switch 3-8 (the top bit of the third byte) starts the 286 machine's CPU as a V30. A value that is not three bytes is refused, and the default is used. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.extra_memory_mb.about: Memory above the first megabyte, in MB. The default is 13. Some programs refuse to start with too little, and a few old ones with too much. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.extra_memory_mb.about_2: Memory above the first megabyte, in MB, up to the 13 a 286 PC-9801 can have. The default is 13. Some programs refuse to start with too little, and a few old ones with too much. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.floppies_at_start.about: Which drives have a floppy in them when the machine is switched on. Drives 1 and 2, the default, get the first and second floppies of the project. The PC-98 boots a formatted floppy in either drive before the hard disk, so to boot the hard disk with floppies listed, choose Drive 1 only (when the first floppy does not boot) or None. An empty drive takes the floppy its selector is on (the first for drive 1, the second for drive 2) when its Swap input is pressed, and the Eject inputs empty a drive at any time.
texts.setting.floppy_seek_sounds.about: Plays the sound of the floppy drive's head moving, as NP2kai can. It also makes a seek take as long as a real drive's head takes to move, which NP2kai ties to the sound, so it changes how long disk access takes. Off by default, as in NP2kai. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.font_file.about: Which file holds the PC-98's characters: FONT.ROM, a dump of the character ROM, or FONT.BMP, the picture form some emulators use. One of them is needed: without it the machine shows no text. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.gdc_type.about: Which graphics display controller chip the machine has. The uPD7220, the default, is the earlier chip; the uPD72020 of later machines draws some graphics modes differently, which a few games rely on. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.machine.about: Which CPU the PC-98 has. PC9821 is NP2kai's IA-32 build (np21kai), which runs everything from the PC-9801 to the Windows-era PC-9821, with hard disks on IDE and a CD-ROM drive. PC98 is its 286 build (np2kai), the older PC-9801 with a 286, hard disks on SASI and no CD-ROM drive; some old software only runs right on it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.memory_switches.about: The eight memory switches the PC-98 keeps in its battery-backed memory, as eight bytes in hexadecimal (NP2kai writes them the same way in its np2.cfg). The default, 48 05 04 08 01 00 00 6E, is NP2kai's. They hold settings MS-DOS's SWITCH command changes, such as the printer, the RS-232C line and the text screen. Software that changes them changes them in the machine, and they go back to this value when the machine is switched on or reset. A value that is not eight bytes is refused, and the default is used. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.model.about: Which PC-98 the machine is. VX is a PC-9801VX, the model NP2kai starts as. VM is the older PC-9801VM. EPSON is an Epson PC-286 compatible, which some software checks for. The CPU is the one the Machine setting chose. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.monitor.about: The display mode the frame rate is counted in. One frame is one picture of the PC-98's display, and its rate depends on the mode: 24khz is the usual 640x400 mode at 56.42 frames a second, 31khz is the PC-9821's 640x400 mode at 70.32, 31khz480 its 640x480 mode at 60.14, and 15khz the 640x200 mode of the first PC-9801s, at 61.46. The machine starts in the 24khz mode, or in the 15khz one when 15khz is chosen (it sets DIP switch 1-1, which tells the machine a 15 kHz monitor is fitted), and software switches mode by itself. Choose the mode the game runs in, so the movie's times are right. It decides how a movie's frames are counted, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pci_bus.about: Whether the IA-32 machine has a PCI bus, as the later PC-9821 models do, and whether its BIOS offers the BIOS32 service PCI software looks for. Off by default, as in NP2kai. Windows 95 and later use it to find PCI devices. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pegc_plane_mode.about: Whether the PC-9821's 256-colour graphics (the PEGC) also offer their plane mode, which a few programs use instead of the usual packed mode. Off by default, as in NP2kai. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.rhythm_samples.about: Where the drums of the sound chip (YM2608) come from. WAV files, the default, are the six 2608_*.WAV recordings PC-98 emulators share. YM2608 ROM is the chip's own drum ROM, as MAME dumps it (ym2608_adpcm_rom.bin, in MAME's ym2608.zip), played as the chip plays them: the same drums, without the noise and ringing at the end of the recordings, and within about 1.5 dB of their loudness. Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with either.
texts.setting.sound_board.about: Which sound board is fitted. The PC-9801-86 is the most common and the default; it has FM, SSG, rhythm and PCM sound. Games usually say which boards they support. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sound_generator.about: Which code makes the sound of the FM sound chips. NP2 is NP2kai's own; fmgen is the YM2608 emulator NP2kai's builds start with. They differ in the balance: fmgen's SSG (most games' sound effects) is about 6 dB louder next to the FM music. Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with either.
texts.setting.start_time.about: The date and time the machine's calendar clock shows when it is switched on, exactly as written here. Chimera keeps every date in UTC, but a PC-98's clock has no time zone: it holds the local time it was set to, so write the time you want the machine to show, with no conversion. The clock then runs with the emulated time, not with the time on your computer. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.volume_adpcm.about: The ADPCM sample channel of the PC-9801-86 and similar boards. The default, 64, is NP2kai's (out of 128). Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.setting.volume_fm.about: The FM music of the sound board's FM chip (and of OPL chips). The default, 64, is NP2kai's (out of 128). Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.setting.volume_master.about: Every sound of the machine together, in per cent. The default, 100, is NP2kai's (out of 100). Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.setting.volume_pcm.about: The PCM sample playback of the PC-9801-86 board. The default, 64, is NP2kai's (out of 128). Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.setting.volume_rhythm.about: The drums of the FM chip (YM2608 rhythm). The default, 64, is NP2kai's (out of 128). Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.setting.volume_ssg.about: The SSG of the FM chip, which most games use for sound effects. The default, 64, is NP2kai's (out of 128). Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.slot.cdrom.help: CD-ROM images for the IDE CD-ROM drive, which only the PC9821 machine has: a .cue sheet with its track files (one .bin for the whole disc or one per track), an .iso, or a MAME .chd (made with chdman createcd). The first is in the drive when the machine starts; the CD Previous, Next, Swap and Eject Disc inputs change it, in the order listed here. A CloneCD .ccd can be converted to .cue and .bin first. A PC-98 cannot start from a CD, so a CD game also needs its boot floppy or a hard disk with its driver.
texts.slot.floppy.help: Floppy disk images (.d88, .fdi, .hdm, .nfd, .dcp, .fdd, .hd4 and the other PC-98 formats). The first is in drive 1 and the second in drive 2 when the machine starts. The order here is the order the Previous, Next and Swap Floppy Disk inputs go through. What the machine writes to a disk stays for the session and can be exported as save data.
texts.slot.hdd.help: Hard disk images (.hdi, .nhd, .thd, .vhd or SL9821's .slh). The first is the first hard disk (IDE on the PC9821 machine, SASI on the PC98 one), the one the machine starts from when no floppy is in drive 1. What the machine writes stays for the session and can be exported as save data, and an exported image can be given here to continue from it.
texts.slot.scsi.help: Hard disks on a PC-9801-55 SCSI board, which the machine gets when this list has a disk: Virtual98 .hdd, RaSCSI .hdn and .hds, or .hdi, .nhd and .vhd. The first is SCSI ID 0, the next ID 1 and so on. The machine starts from the first SCSI disk when no floppy is in a drive and there is no IDE or SASI hard disk. What the machine writes stays for the session and can be exported as save data.
